When players who had moved to the city needed a sound that could stand for home, they picked out and standardised one line-up and one repertoire, then recorded it in quantity. Some of the Andean recordings considered most authentic today are in fact a tidying-up done by urban migrants for the market and for identity. The versions in the villages are more scattered and more changeable.
